title: Slain man had been deported; SIU probing fatal shooting by police during drug arrest Suspect had returned to Canada illegally after two removals
article: The 32-year-old man shot dead by police during an undercover drug arrest in an east-end gas station had a string of criminal convictions and was in the country illegally more than a decade after he was first ordered deported from Canada.

Courtney Peters was shot in the chest as plainclothes police officers tried to arrest the occupants of a car at a Petro-Canada gas station at Ellesmere Rd. and Victoria Park Ave. about 10 30 p.m. Thursday.
The province's Special Investigation Unit has assigned eight investigators to the case, designating one subject and five witness officers.

The officers were involved in the attempted takedown when there was "a confrontation," SIU spokesperson Rose Bliss said yesterday. Witnesses said plainclothes officers driving a Jeep and a gray Pontiac Grand Prix boxed in a black Infiniti driven by Peters. The G35 sports car collided with the rear end of the Grand Prix. The Infiniti's wheels were aligned to steer around the police vehicle.

A source said the officer fired twice and that no other shots were fired, contradicting at least one witness's recollection of the number of shots. The source added that no other weapons were found. A 22-year-old passenger was arrested.

A crowd quickly gathered after the shooting as investigators interviewed potential witnesses, including several who yelled at police while Peters lay sprawled on the pavement next to the car, which was leased to his girlfriend. "I saw the guy shoot into the driver's side of the car (the Infiniti)," one witness told the Star's Henry Stancu.

He said he was standing at the back of the gas bar near a fence when he heard a commotion and saw the sports car ramming the Grand Prix in a bid to get away. "After he ran into the car, that's when the shooting happened," said the man, who identified himself only as Jay.
The circumstances of the drug investigation are not known, but a source said Peters was under surveillance for suspected cocaine trafficking.

In 1996, Peters, then 24, was living in Mississauga when he was charged and later convicted of forcing his way into a North York woman's apartment, where he bound, gagged and threatened to electrocute her. A Star story at the time said he was out on bail and prohibited by court order from having any contact with the woman and her 4-month-old child.

Two years later, he was deported to Jamaica on a deportation order issued in 1993, but later illegally returned to Canada and was reportedly arrested in 2000 by the OPP in a car containing drugs, a handgun and burglary tools. He was once again removed from Canada in November 2002, an immigration official confirmed.

The SIU, which investigates cases of serious injury or death involving police, is now probing the province's seventh fatal police shooting of the year; there was just one in all of 2003. Five of this year's shootings were by Toronto officers. In each of the previous four cases, the SIU ruled the shootings were legally justified and no charges were laid.

The earlier victims include Sugston Anthony (Tony) Brookes, 45, shot dead Aug. 25 outside Union Station after holding a young woman hostage during the morning rush hour. On June 13, O'brien Christopher Reid, 26, was shot dead in Edwards Gardens, and one officer was hit in crossfire. A month earlier, 17-year-old Jeffrey Reodica was shot and killed by a police officer, and in January, Antonio Bellon, 63, was shot dead by an officer in Dufferin Ave. and Rogers Rd. area.
